subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, and what minimal public config/state surface should it expose first?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent those product boundaries or defaults.

options.title: Design additive core pool routing
options.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool routing contract that preserves current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

options.title: Phase narrow requirements under this tracker
options.body: Keep this issue canonical while folding the related key-bucket, rotation-depth, model-auth binding, and pace-governance issues into separate phased acceptance criteria.

options.title: Defer to sidecar or plugin seam
options.body: Keep current core behavior and recommend external sidecars or future plugin/provider hooks until maintainers decide the native config/state surface is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design additive core pool routing
recommendation.body: Define a minimal opt-in provider/auth pool routing contract that preserves current session-sticky defaults and starts with one observable strategy before expanding to quota, bucket, and weighting semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting product/config boundary decision, and the history evidence ties steipete to both auth-profile storage and recent auth-order work.
